prior_art_establishes: Discrete phenotypic character construction can be ambiguous; state aggregation is formally tied to Markov lumpability and hierarchical/hidden structure.
overlap_with_current_program: Directly relevant theoretical prior art: coarse-state recoding is not automatically innocuous.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Apply an explicit empirical partition-competition/falsification design to flower-colour macroevolution across multiple independent radiations rather than introduce coding sensitivity as a new general concept.

prior_art_establishes: Recoding/aggregating states can fail to retain the Markov property; formal likelihood-ratio lumpability tests exist for nucleotide data.
overlap_with_current_program: Supports the broader warning that aggregation can distort phylogenetic inference.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Current phenotype analysis is an empirical organization/partition-specificity audit, not a formal lumpability test; extending formal lumpability to identified phenotype CTMCs is future work.

prior_art_establishes: Pollinator-perceptual colour categories can combine distinct pigment combinations, so a colour category need not share one evolutionary history; authors avoid ASR for those categories.
overlap_with_current_program: Very close conceptual prior art for colour-state aliasing.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Current program directly quantifies competing state partitions rather than only warning against one problematic coding, and repeats the test across multiple radiations.

prior_art_establishes: Within-taxon colour polymorphism is a comparative-method challenge; separate polymorphic and monomorphic treatments are analyzed.
overlap_with_current_program: Direct prior art for coding/sampling sensitivity in one of the reanalysed systems.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Use the source-native states to run a pre-frozen nested fine-state test and then exhaustive alternative-partition specificity controls without treating posterior trees as biological replication.

prior_art_establishes: Flower colour/pigment are represented with multiple binary and polymorphic characters; model overfitting can depend on representation and ER is used when ARD behaves pathologically.
overlap_with_current_program: Prior art that flower-colour inference depends on representation/model choices.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Cross-radiation exhaustive partition ranking and prospective external validation/falsification are not supplied by this study.

prior_art_establishes: Similar visible red flower states repeatedly arise through anthocyanin, carotenoid, or combined biochemical pathways; pigment-pathway use itself has phylogenetic signal.
overlap_with_current_program: Shows visible endpoint and biochemical state are not one-to-one and that finer mechanistic states can carry phylogenetic structure.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Current macro layer tests phenotype-state granularity directly and does not claim visible-state/mechanism non-equivalence as new.

prior_art_establishes: Camellia ancestral flower colour is reconstructed using yellow/white/red states with white inferred ancestral.
overlap_with_current_program: Example of the standard fixed categorical coding whose robustness matters for the project.
remaining_distinct_contribution: Current accepted-species audit prospectively compares all W/A/Y bipartitions across two topology and two colour-coding treatments and finds a mixed best partition.

Three independent radiations retain fine-state phylogenetic organization; exhaustive alternative bipartitions reject a shared privileged coarse boundary, and a prospectively tested Camellia yellow-axis candidate is mixed. The contribution is the flower-colour-specific multi-radiation falsification architecture and result, not the general idea that coding matters.
